safety-monitor.note_autorestart: customer-safety Intercom sweep. A blind re-run cannot double-TAG (the apply is idempotent and an already-tagged conversation is skipped before the classifier runs) and it CAN duplicate an ALERT: alerting is deliberately at-least-once, because SNS publish and the Intercom tag are two non-atomic writes and the alert-then-tag order puts the whole failure budget on the duplicate side. So a restart may re-alert a conversation whose alert succeeded but whose tag did not. That is the intended trade -- a human told twice is a cheap annoyance, a human told zero times is what this job exists to prevent -- and it is why restarting is safe, not because alerts are deduplicated. Silence here is the failure this job exists to end, so LATE must page.

nightly-fleet-medic.note: Nightly Fleet Medic (otchealth-mcp-server, cron '0 8 * * *'): opens a fix issue when main CI is red. It does NOT read _HEARTBEAT (checked 2026-10-07: nightly-medic.mjs triages CI, and skills/fleet-medic/medic.mjs scans agent memory health), so it is not the silence monitor, and it has no AWS role to beat with, so the GitHub schedule history is its only witness. otchealth-mcp-server is a PUBLIC repo, so that history is readable with this monitor's own GITHUB_TOKEN or anonymously and needs no PAT; the optional repo secret FLEET_WATCH_GH_TOKEN is only a fallback should the repo ever go private. If neither read works the row reports UNWITNESSED, which pages and names the fix. To give it a beat instead, a role with s3:PutObject on _HEARTBEAT/nightly-fleet-medic.json would be needed (an IAM change). GitHub runs it 5-9h late; gaps of up to 27h were observed 2026-09-29..10-07.

aws-health-monitor.note: Hourly read-only AWS health report (gateway ECS service and base URL, RDS, OpenSearch) in otchealth-cto, cron '17 * * * *'. GitHub throttles it to about 4 to 6 real runs a day (42 scheduled runs 2026-09-28..10-07, longest gap 9h), hence a 6h cadence and an 18h limit. It has no pager of its own, so a run-failing check is its pager. otchealth-cto is PRIVATE, so its Actions history cannot be read without a PAT; the row is witnessed by the job's own BEAT instead: the workflow's final step (if: always(), never turns the job red) writes this beat with the job's own AWS role, ok on success and fail on failure. That needs s3:GetObject and s3:PutObject on _HEARTBEAT/aws-health-monitor.json in bucket otchealth-brain-dr-55c84f6b for that role (the role in repo variable AWS_OIDC_ROLE_ARN_RECOVERY_CONSOLE); until it is granted the row reports UNWITNESSED, which pages and names the fix. gh_workflow stays as an optional fallback for the day FLEET_WATCH_GH_TOKEN is set.

stale-pr-closer.note: Close stale PRs and branches (.github/workflows/stale.yml, actions/stale, cron '17 9 * * *', daily). PR hygiene only: no AWS role, no pager, silent by design when nothing is stale, so the GitHub schedule history of this repo (read with the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN) is its only witness. A dead cron would let PR and branch sprawl return unnoticed. Observed gaps between daily runs reach 27h45m (2026-10-04 14:48 to 10-05 18:33), hence the 36h limit. The identical file also runs in otchealth-cto (a private repo); that copy is not registered because reading a private repo's runs needs the optional FLEET_WATCH_GH_TOKEN.

sentinel-watchdog.note: The watchdog of this very monitor (.github/workflows/sentinel-watchdog.yml, cron '50 13 * * *', daily). It pages when nightly-fleet-sentinels.yml has not completed a run for 26h; this row makes the monitor page when the watchdog's own cron goes quiet, so neither can go dark unseen. Witnessed by the GitHub schedule history (same repo, GITHUB_TOKEN). armed 2026-10-09 (the day after the expected merge) gives it one limit (36h) from that date to show its first scheduled run, because the monitor's first run after the merge usually comes before the watchdog's first (GitHub starts both hours late) and a manual dispatch is not a scheduled run. armed only applies while the row has shown no proof of life yet; once it has, silence is STALE as for any other row. If this lands after the morning of 2026-10-09 UTC, set armed to the merge date.

codex-continuity-lane.note: Codex API continuity lane (.github/workflows/codex-run.yml, cron '17 9 * * 1', WEEKLY on Mondays): the API-backed hedge worker running one bounded canary task. It has no AWS role and no pager, so a red or missing run was visible to nobody; the GitHub schedule history is its witness. The 11 day limit (15840 min) tolerates a late Monday run and pages when a whole week is skipped. As of 2026-10-07 its scheduled runs fail at the 'Persist changes to a draft pull request' step, so this row reports FAILING until a scheduled run goes green, which is accurate. The same lane also runs in otchealth-cto (private) and otchealth-mcp-server; those copies are not registered here.
